mainTopic: How mourning for a parent is stricter than for other relatives, especially in קריעה, and how the community mourns a חכם, an אב בית דין and a נשיא.
overview: This amud continues a ברייתא that compares mourning for most relatives with mourning for a father or mother. Again and again, something that is optional for other relatives is required for a parent, or a parent's version is stricter. Examples are cutting back on business, baring a shoulder, haircuts, going to happy events, and many details of קריעה (tearing the garment). A story about two גדולי הדור leads to a קשיא about which sage was the mourner. רבה בר בר חנה explains what kind of happy event the thirty-day rule covers, and in אמימר's version the גמרא settles a clash by telling apart hosting first from hosting friends back. רבי אבהו brings פסוקים for the size of the tear and for רבי יהודה's view that a tear must cut through the garment's edge. רבי יוחנן and רב חסדא add that for a parent, and also for a נשיא, one tears by hand and on the outer garment. The amud ends with how the community mourns a חכם, an אב בית דין and a נשיא, and that teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: For a father or mother, the mourner must cut back
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ruling: for most relatives cutting back is optional, but for a father or mother the mourner must cut back.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If he wishes, he may] reduce it. For his father or mother, he must reduce it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a sentence in a ברייתא. It finishes the rule that for a father or mother, the mourner must cut back on his business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first word finishes the 'optional' half of the rule for ordinary relatives, which began earlier on the daf. The second half sets up the pattern for this whole section: what is optional for other relatives is required for a father or mother.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts back, reduces (here, his business activity)
For his father or his mother

phrases.english: [if he wishes,] he reduces [it];
phrases.notes: This word finishes a sentence from just before here: for other relatives, cutting back on business is up to the mourner.

phrases.english: for his father or his mother, he reduces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a father or mother, a mourner must cut back on his business.

steps.title: Baring the shoulder: optional for most, required for parents
steps.stepSummary: For all other relatives חליצה (baring a shoulder) is optional. For a father or mother it is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other dead relatives, if he wants he bares his shoulder, and if he wants he does not. For his father or mother, he bares it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second rule with the same pattern. Baring one shoulder in mourning is a choice for most relatives but a must for a parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats the earlier structure with a new practice, חליצה. The difference again depends only on who died. A parent calls for the fuller expression of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: Bares (removes his garment from one shoulder) as a sign of mourning
If he wants
All the other deceased relatives

phrases.english: For all the other dead,
if he wants, he bares [his shoulder]; if he wants, he does not bare it.
phrases.notes: He takes his garment off one shoulder as a sign of mourning.

phrases.english: For his father or his mother, he bares it.

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting back on business and baring the shoulder are optional for most relatives but required for a father or mother.
steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן, רָצָה — חוֹלֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel rule using the same 'optional for others, required for parents' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה is optional for other relatives and required for a father or mother.

steps.title: The story of two great leaders and the bared shoulder
steps.stepSummary: A גדול הדור's father died and he wanted to bare his shoulder. Another גדול הדור wanted to join him, so the mourner held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It happened that the father of a leader of the generation died, and he wanted to bare his shoulder. Another leader of the generation who was with him also wanted to bare his shoulder, so he held back and did not bare it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story connected to the rule about baring the shoulder. A mourner for his father chose not to bare his shoulder because his colleague would have done the same out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the last rule, a son should bare his shoulder for his father. Here the mourner held back so that the other great leader would not lower his own dignity by mourning along with him. The story shows that honoring a colleague can affect how this mourning practice is carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: The leading Torah authority of the generation
And he held back
An incident or story

steps.confusionAlert: The one who held back was the mourner himself, not the colleague. He refrained so that his colleague would not bare his shoulder too.

phrases.english: And there was an incident with one great man of the generation
whose father died, and he wanted to bare [his shoulder],

phrases.aramaic: וּבִיקֵּשׁ גְּדוֹל הַדּוֹר אַחֵר שֶׁעִמּוֹ לַחְלוֹץ,
phrases.english: and another great man of the generation who was with him wanted to bare [his shoulder too],
so he held back and did not bare it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life case connected to the rule of חליצה for a father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner may hold back from חליצה for his father so that a great colleague will not bare his shoulder along with him.

steps.title: אביי names the two leaders
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the mourner was רבי and his colleague was רבי יעקב בר אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The great man of the generation was רבי, and the great man with him was רבי יעקב בר אחא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us who the two unnamed leaders in the story were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not name the people. אביי identifies the mourner as רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) and the colleague as רבי יעקב בר אחא.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of Babylonia
Here, רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: אביי said:
The great man of the generation was רבי,

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹל הַדּוֹר שֶׁעִמּוֹ — רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא.
phrases.english: and the great man of the generation with him was רבי יעקב בר אחא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the people in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourner was רבי, and the colleague was רבי יעקב בר אחא.

steps.title: A second version swaps the two leaders
steps.stepSummary: Some say the mourner was רבי יעקב בר אחא and his colleague was רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: The great man of the generation was רבי יעקב בר אחא, and the great man with him was רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of אביי's identification, with the roles reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבי יעקב בר אחא was the mourner, and רבי was the colleague who wanted to bare his shoulder with him. The switch matters: in steps 6 and 7 the גמרא shows that one version fits the story well and the other runs into a difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (introduces a second version)
A sage named here as the other great man

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹל הַדּוֹר — רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא,
phrases.english: The great man of the generation was רבי יעקב בר אחא,
and the great man of the generation with him was רבי.

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows a mourner holding back from חליצה out of respect for a great colleague. The two versions differ on which sage was the mourner, and the next steps test which version fits.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: גְּדוֹל הַדּוֹר — רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of step 4 with the roles reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourner was רבי יעקב בר אחא, and the colleague was רבי.

steps.title: The first version fits the story well
steps.stepSummary: If the great colleague was רבי, it makes sense that the mourner held back from baring his shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says the great man of the generation who was with him was רבי, that explains why he held back and did not bare his shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It first shows that one version of the story makes good sense, so it can then ask about the other version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the colleague was רבי, the נשיא. The mourner did not want to make the נשיא bare his shoulder too, so he held back himself. That reason is easy to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works fine (opens a 'this version works, but…' challenge)
According to the one who says
Held back / refrained
Bared (his shoulder by pulling back his garment)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
that the great man of the generation who was with him was רבי,
phrases.notes: 'With him' means the colleague who came to join the mourner, not the mourner himself.

phrases.english: that is why he held back and did not bare his shoulder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two versions from steps 4 and 5 against the story in step 3, starting with the version that works.

steps.title: Why would רבי hold back if his father was the נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: In the other version the mourner was רבי. His father רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was the נשיא, and everyone must bare a shoulder for a נשיא, so there was no reason to stop the colleague. The question is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says the colleague was רבי יעקב בר אחא, why did the mourner hold back and not bare his shoulder? רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was the נשיא, and everyone is required to bare a shoulder for him! It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second version of the story. It finds no good answer, so it ends with קשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mourner is רבי, and the one who died is his father, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who was the נשיא. Everyone has to bare a shoulder when a נשיא dies, so רבי יעקב בר אחא would have had to do it anyway. Holding back to spare him makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
The head of the Jewish people / of the סנהדרין
Everyone
It is difficult (a question left without an answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Here קשיא at the end does not mean the opinion is thrown out. It means the גמרא has no answer for now.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא,
phrases.english: But according to the one who says it was רבי יעקב בר אחא,
phrases.notes: In this version רבי יעקב בר אחא is the colleague, so רבי is the mourner.

phrases.english: why did he hold back and not bare his shoulder?

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל נָשִׂיא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was the נשיא,
and everyone is required to bare a shoulder!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'granted… but' challenge that step 6 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version that makes רבי the mourner and רבי יעקב בר אחא the colleague
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone must bare a shoulder for a נשיא, so the colleague had to do it anyway. There was no reason for the mourner to hold back on his account.

steps.title: When a mourner may cut his hair and go to happy events
steps.stepSummary: For other relatives, a mourner cuts his hair and goes to happy events after thirty days. For a parent, he waits until his friends scold him about his hair, and he stays away from happy events for twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other dead relatives, he cuts his hair after thirty days. For his father or mother, he waits until his friends scold him. For all other dead relatives, he enters a house of celebration after thirty days. For his father or mother, he waits twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא it was quoting and brings its next rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same pattern as steps 1 and 2: mourning for a parent is stricter. For haircuts, the parent case has no fixed number of days. It depends on when friends say his hair has gotten too long. For happy events, thirty days becomes twelve months.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts his hair
His friends scold him (about his long hair)
A house of celebration / a happy event
Twelve months

steps.whatToRemember: Other relatives: thirty days for both haircuts and happy events. A parent: no haircut until friends scold him, and no happy events for twelve months.

phrases.english: For all the other dead relatives,
he cuts his hair after thirty days;
for his father or his mother,
he waits until his friends scold him.
phrases.notes: They tell him his hair has grown too long, and only then may he cut it.

phrases.english: For all the other dead relatives,

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנָס לְבֵית הַשִּׂמְחָה לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: he enters a house of celebration after thirty days;
for his father or his mother,
after twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן מִסְתַּפֵּר לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the story and goes back to the ברייתא from steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Other relatives: haircut and happy events after thirty days. A parent: haircut only once friends scold him, and happy events after twelve months.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: the thirty days is for friendly get-togethers
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says the thirty-day permission covers friendly get-togethers, not big celebrations like weddings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: this refers to a friendly get-together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה explains which kind of happy event the thirty-day rule is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He narrows the rule. After thirty days, a mourner for other relatives may go to friendly get-together meals. He does not say this allows big celebrations like weddings that soon.

keyTerms.meaning: A friendly get-together (friends taking turns hosting meals)

phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה said:
And this refers to a friendly get-together.
phrases.notes: He means the 'thirty days' for a house of celebration is talking about meals among friends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'house of celebration' from the ברייתא in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirty-day permission covers friendly get-togethers.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists celebrations and get-togethers separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'for a celebration and for a get-together, thirty days.' That suggests 'celebration' means even big events, which goes against רבה בר בר חנה. The difficulty is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: 'For a celebration and for a friendly get-together, thirty days.' It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר בר חנה from a ברייתא and does not answer, so it ends with קשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names a get-together as a separate item from a celebration. So a plain 'celebration' must mean bigger events, such as weddings. Thirty days applies to those too, against רבה בר בר חנה's narrower reading.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא suggests thirty days applies even to big celebrations, and רבה בר בר חנה's narrow reading is left with a קשיא.

phrases.english: They challenged him:
'And for a celebration and for a friendly get-together, thirty days.'
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה בר בר חנה's narrow reading from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר בר חנה's claim that the thirty days applies only to friendly get-togethers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists 'celebration' separately from 'get-together' and gives both thirty days. So big celebrations are allowed after thirty days too.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge to רבה בר בר חנה stays unanswered.

steps.title: A second version: a mourner may join a friendly get-together right away
steps.stepSummary: אמימר reports רבה בר בר חנה differently: a mourner may go to a friendly get-together immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר taught it this way. רבה בר בר חנה said: for a friendly get-together, a mourner may go in right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבה בר בר חנה's teaching. In this version he is even more lenient: a friendly get-together is allowed at once, with no thirty-day wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רבה בר בר חנה said the thirty days apply to get-togethers, not to weddings. Here אמימר's version says get-togethers need no waiting at all. This sets up a new clash with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: taught it this way, a different version of a teaching
a friendly get-together among companions
right away, immediately

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with step 9. It is another report of what רבה בר בר חנה himself said.

phrases.english: Ameimar taught it this way:
Rabba bar bar Chana said:
And for a get-together of friends
one is allowed to go in right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of רבה בר בר חנה's statement, which was challenged in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In אמימר's version, a mourner may attend a friendly get-together immediately, with no thirty-day wait.

steps.title: A ברייתא requires thirty days even for a get-together
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says both a celebration and a get-together need thirty days, which goes against 'right away.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: for a celebration, thirty days, and for a get-together, thirty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a get-together needs a thirty-day wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה said 'right away.' The ברייתא clearly says 'thirty days' for a get-together. These two cannot both be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it taught in a ברייתא, an opening for a challenge
thirty days

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
for a celebration, thirty days,
and for a get-together, thirty days!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 11 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר בר חנה's ruling, in אמימר's version, that a get-together is allowed immediately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly requires thirty days for a get-together, which contradicts 'immediately.'

steps.title: Hosting first versus paying friends back
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means a gathering the mourner starts as host. רבה בר בר חנה means a gathering where it is his turn to host his friends back.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's not difficult: this one is about a first gathering, that one is about a return gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the cases. Each source is talking about a different kind of get-together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mourner is the first to host, he must wait thirty days, as the ברייתא says. If his friends already hosted him and now he owes them, he may host right away, as רבה בר בר חנה says. Paying back is an obligation, so he does not delay it.

keyTerms.meaning: it's not difficult, an opening for an answer
a first gathering, where the mourner hosts first
a return gathering, where he pays his friends back

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, a mourner for other relatives waits thirty days before hosting a get-together first, but he may return his friends' hospitality right away.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about a first gathering,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא's case: the mourner hosts first, so he waits thirty days.

phrases.english: that one is about a return gathering.
phrases.notes: This is רבה בר בר חנה's case: his friends already hosted him, so now it's his turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בַּאֲרִיסוּתָא, הָא בְּפוּרְעֲנוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources speak about different kinds of gatherings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to speak about the same get-together, so they seemed to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's thirty days apply to a gathering the mourner starts. 'Immediately' applies to a gathering where he is paying back.

steps.title: How big the tear is: a טפח, or until the heart shows
steps.stepSummary: For other relatives one tears a טפח. For a parent one tears until his heart shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other dead relatives one tears a טפח. For his father or mother he tears until he exposes his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and continues with a new topic: the size of the tear (קריעה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the pattern of the ברייתא, where a parent gets stricter mourning than other relatives. For others a small tear of one טפח is enough. For a parent the tear must be big enough to show the chest.

keyTerms.meaning: tears his garment as a sign of mourning
a handbreadth, about the width of four fingers
until he exposes his heart, meaning his chest

phrases.english: For all the other dead relatives
one tears a handbreadth,
for his father and for his mother
until he exposes his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן קוֹרֵעַ טֶפַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 8 with a new topic, the size of קריעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tear one טפח for other relatives. For a parent, tear until the heart is exposed.

steps.title: The source for a טפח: דוד grabbed his clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns the טפח from the פסוק about דוד grabbing his clothes, because you can't grab less than a טפח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: what is the פסוק? "And David took hold of his clothes and tore them," and you cannot take hold of less than a טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a פסוק as the source for the one-טפח tear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says דוד took hold of his clothes and tore them. A grip needs at least a טפח of cloth, so the tear was at least a טפח.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the פסוק, asking for the source
grabbing or taking hold

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: What is the verse?
"And David took hold of his clothes and tore them,"
and taking hold is not less than a handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a scriptural source for the טפח rule in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a tear for other relatives is one טפח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 1:11. דוד 'took hold' of his clothes, and a grip needs at least a טפח.

steps.title: Tearing only the top garment or all of them
steps.stepSummary: For other relatives one tears only the outer garment, even if he wears ten. For a parent he tears all of them, but not tearing the undershirt doesn't ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other dead relatives, even if he wears ten shirts, he tears only the top one. For his father or mother he tears all of them. But his undershirt does not hold back the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with which garments must be torn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again a parent is treated more strictly. For others only the outer layer is torn. For a parent every layer is torn, with one exception: if the undershirt is left whole, he has still done the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: shirts or garments
the top, outer garment
his undershirt, worn next to the skin
does not hold back, the מצוה still counts without it

steps.whatToRemember: For a parent, mourning is stricter at every point: a longer wait for get-togethers, a tear until the heart shows, and tearing all the garments.

phrases.english: For all the other dead relatives
even if he is wearing ten shirts,
he tears only the top one,
for his father and for his mother
he tears all of them.
And his undershirt does not hold it back.
phrases.notes: He means that even if he doesn't tear his undershirt, the tearing still counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן אֲפִילּוּ לָבוּשׁ עֲשָׂרָה חֲלוּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's קריעה laws, moving from the size of the tear to which garments are torn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other relatives tear only the outer garment. For a parent tear all of them, though leaving the undershirt whole does not ruin the מצוה.

steps.title: Men and women both tear
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the laws of קריעה apply equally to a man and a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both a man and a woman tear their clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds that everything just said about tearing clothes applies to women too, not only men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 described tearing the outer garment, or all garments for a parent. Now the ברייתא makes clear that a woman also has the חיוב of קריעה. This sets up the next step, which asks how a woman can tear without being immodest.

keyTerms.meaning: Both a man and a woman: the same law applies to both
Tearing one's clothes as a sign of mourning

phrases.english: Both a man and a woman [must tear].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the tearing rules of step 16 to women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in קריעה just like men.

steps.title: How a woman tears modestly
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a woman first tears her inner garment and turns the tear to her back, then tears her outer garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: A woman tears her inner garment and turns it around to her back. Then she goes back and tears her outer garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains the way a woman should tear so that she does not end up uncovered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a woman tore every layer in front, her chest would show. So she tears the inner layer, turns it so the tear is at her back, and then tears the outer layer in front. The front tear only shows the untorn back of the inner garment.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner (lower) garment
The outer (upper) garment
To her back

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
The woman tears the inner garment
and turns it around to her back,
and then she tears the outer garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the woman's obligation from step 17 is carried out modestly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman tears the inner garment, turns the tear to her back, and then tears the outer garment.

steps.title: Tearing through the edge of the garment
steps.stepSummary: For other relatives, tearing right through the garment's edge is optional. For a parent, it is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other dead relatives, if he wants he tears right through the edge of his garment, and if he wants he does not. For his father or mother, he must tear through the edge.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a new detail: whether the tear has to go all the way through the finished border of the garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing through the border makes the tear clearly separate from the normal neck opening, so everyone sees it is a real tear. For other relatives this is up to the mourner. For a parent it is a must, which matches the extra strictness for parents in steps 14 and 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates: tears right through, cutting the edge apart
The edge or border of the garment, near the neck opening
If he wants

phrases.english: For all the other dead relatives,
if he wants, he tears through the edge of his garment,
and if he wants, he does not tear through.
For his father and his mother, he must tear through.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן, רָצָה מַבְדִּיל קַמֵּי שָׂפָה שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way the tear for a parent is stricter than for other relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tearing through the edge is optional for other relatives and required for a parent.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a tear without cutting the edge hardly counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says any tear that does not go through the edge is only a meaningless tear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Any tear that does not cut through the edge of the garment is nothing more than a silly, meaningless tear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the 'optional' part of step 19. To him, a tear must always go through the edge, even for other relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא let the mourner choose for other relatives. רבי יהודה says a tear that does not cut the border looks like an ordinary rip, not a mourning tear. So for him, tearing through the edge is always needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A meaningless or silly tear that doesn't count as real mourning
It is nothing but

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל קְרִיעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל קַמֵּי שָׂפָה שֶׁלּוֹ —
phrases.english: Any tear that does not cut through the edge of his garment
is nothing but a meaningless tear.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל קְרִיעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַבְדִּיל קַמֵּי שָׂפָה שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 19, which made cutting the edge optional for other relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהודה, every proper קריעה must cut through the edge of the garment.

steps.title: The פסוק behind רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns from 'he tore them into two pieces' that the tear must look like it splits the garment in two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is רבי יהודה's reason? Because it says, 'He grabbed his clothes and tore them into two pieces.' From the word 'he tore them,' don't I already know they are in two? So the extra words teach that the clothes must look like they are torn into two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a source from a פסוק for רבי יהודה's view in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'he tore them' already tells us the garment was torn, so 'into two pieces' seems extra. The extra words teach that the tear must be clear enough to look like the garment is split in two. That only happens if the tear goes through the edge.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
From the plain meaning of what is said
They look like, appear

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי אבהו used a פסוק about דוד (שמואל ב 1:11) in step 15 for the size of a טפח. Here he uses a different פסוק (מלכים ב 2:12) with similar wording, 'he took hold of his clothes,' to teach a different rule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: 'He took hold of his clothes'
'and tore them into two pieces.'
From the fact that it says 'and he tore them,'
don't I already know that they are in two?
Rather, it teaches that they must look torn as if in two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from a פסוק for רבי יהודה's ruling in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's rule that a tear must cut through the garment's edge.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra words 'לשנים קרעים' in מלכים ב 2:12 teach that the tear must look like it splits the garment in two.

steps.title: When the tear may be stitched up
steps.stepSummary: For other relatives you may loosely stitch after seven days and sew properly after thirty. For a parent you may loosely stitch after thirty and never sew properly. A woman may loosely stitch right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other dead relatives, he may loosely stitch the tear after seven days and properly sew it after thirty days. For his father or mother, he may loosely stitch after thirty days and may never properly sew it. A woman may loosely stitch it right away, because of her dignity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on to say how long the tear has to stay open before it may be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of fixing: a rough, loose stitch (שולל) and a neat, full repair (מאחה). For a parent both levels wait longer, and a full repair is never allowed. A woman is an exception: she may loosely stitch at once so she is not seen in torn clothes.

keyTerms.meaning: Stitches loosely with big, rough stitches
Sews the tear neatly and properly closed
Right away, immediately
Because of her dignity

steps.whatToRemember: For a parent, every part of קריעה is stricter: you tear until the heart shows, tear all the garments, must cut through the edge, wait thirty days to stitch loosely, and may never sew it properly. A woman tears too, but in a modest way, and may loosely stitch right away.
steps.confusionAlert: שולל and מאחה are not the same thing. שולל is just a rough, temporary stitch. מאחה is a real, neat repair. For a parent, only the rough stitch is ever allowed.

phrases.english: For all the other dead relatives,
he may loosely stitch after seven days,
and properly sew it after thirty days.
For his father and his mother,
he may loosely stitch after thirty days,
and he may never properly sew it.
And a woman may loosely stitch it right away,
because of her dignity.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּל הַמֵּתִים כּוּלָּן שׁוֹלֵל לְאַחַר שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list of קריעה rules, now about repairing the tear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Other relatives: loose stitch after 7 days, full repair after 30. Parent: loose stitch after 30, never a full repair. A woman: loose stitch right away.

steps.title: Tearing by hand or with a tool
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: for other relatives you may tear by hand or with a tool, but for a parent you must tear by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: for all other dead relatives, a person may tear by hand if he wants, or with a tool if he wants. For his father or mother, he must tear by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רבי יוחנן about how the tear is made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing with a tool can be neat and careful, so the garment is less damaged. Tearing by hand is rougher and shows more grief. For a parent, only the stronger form is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings)
Tears (the mourner's garment)
By hand
With a tool or utensil

phrases.english: When Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
For all the dead,
phrases.notes: He means all other relatives you mourn for, not a parent.

phrases.english: if he wants, he tears by hand;
if he wants, he tears with a tool.
For his father or his mother — by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way that tearing for a parent is stricter than for other relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other relatives, tearing may be by hand or with a tool; for a parent, it must be by hand.

steps.title: Inner garment or outer garment
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא reports in the name of רבי יוחנן: for other relatives you tear on the inside, but for a parent you tear on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: for all other dead relatives, one tears on the inside. For his father or mother, he tears on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second rule of רבי יוחנן, this time about which garment gets torn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For other relatives, tearing an inner layer is enough. For a parent, the tear must be on the outer garment, where everyone can see it. Once again, the parent gets the stronger, more public form of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: On the inside (an inner garment)
On the outside (the outer garment)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
For all the other dead — on the inside;
phrases.notes: He means an inner layer of clothing, not necessarily the top layer people see.

phrases.aramaic: עַל אָבִיו וְעַל אִמּוֹ — קוֹרֵעַ מִבַּחוּץ.
phrases.english: for his father or his mother — he tears on the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן, again making tearing for a parent stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other relatives one may tear an inner garment; for a parent one must tear the outer garment.

steps.title: A נשיא is treated like a parent
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the same strict tearing rules apply when a נשיא dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: and the same is true for a נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds that when the leader of the generation, the נשיא, dies, people tear the way they would for a parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן ("and likewise") links the נשיא to the parent rules just mentioned. So tearing for a נשיא must also be strict, like tearing for a father or mother. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise; the same rule applies
The head of the Jewish community and of the סנהדרין

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: And likewise for the Nasi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the parent rules of רבי יוחנן to a נשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tearing for a נשיא follows the same strict rules as tearing for a parent.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to limit the comparison to sewing only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא that says others are like a parent only for the rule of sewing. Doesn't that include the נשיא?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: "They were made equal to his father and mother only for proper sewing." Doesn't this mean even the נשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב חסדא's claim that a נשיא is like a parent for tearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that other important people match a parent in only one detail: you may never sew the tear properly. If that includes the נשיא, then in other details, like tearing by hand or on the outside, the נשיא is not like a parent. That would go against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא)
Were made equal
Proper, careful sewing of the tear
Is it not so that...? (pushing a reading of the source)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
They were not made equal to his father and mother
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about tearing for other important people. They match a parent only in this one detail.

phrases.english: except for proper sewing alone.
Is it not so that this applies even to the Nasi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's statement in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a נשיא is treated like a parent for tearing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says others match a parent only for sewing. If the נשיא is included, he does not match a parent in the other tearing rules.

steps.title: The ברייתא does not include the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about everyone except the נשיא, who is like a parent in every way.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means everyone except the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by limiting the ברייתא to the other important people it lists, not the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's "only for sewing" rule applies to people like a teacher or court leader. The נשיא is left out of that limit, so he is fully like a parent, just as רב חסדא said. The challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for; outside of

steps.whatToRemember: Tearing for a parent is stricter: by hand, on the outer garment, and never sewn properly. A נשיא is treated like a parent in all of these rules. Other important people match a parent only in the sewing rule.

phrases.english: No, it means except for the Nasi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא includes the נשיא, so he matches a parent only for sewing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא leaves out the נשיא, who matches a parent in every tearing rule.

steps.title: When the נשיא died, רב חסדא had the tear shown to everyone
steps.stepSummary: When the נשיא died, רב חסדא told רב חנן בר רבא to stand on an upside-down mortar and show everyone how to tear.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נשיא died. רב חסדא said to רב חנן בר רבא: Turn the mortar upside down, stand on it, and show the tear to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows רב חסדא's rule from Step 25 being carried out in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא held that a נשיא is mourned with the same strict tearing as a parent. So when the נשיא actually died, he made sure the whole crowd saw the correct way to tear. Standing on something high made the tear easy for everyone to see and copy.

keyTerms.meaning: A large mortar, a heavy bowl used for pounding grain
Tearing one's clothing as a sign of mourning
Died (literally, lay down)
Show

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule about the נשיא was not just theory. Everyone was expected to tear for him.

phrases.english: The Nasi died,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Chanan bar Rava:
Turn the mortar over and stand on it,
and show the tear to everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְשִׂיאָה שְׁכֵיב, אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב חסדא, whose view was just defended in Step 27, putting his rule into practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the נשיא dies, everyone tears, and the correct way of tearing should be shown to the public.

steps.title: Which shoulder is uncovered for a חכם, an אב בית דין, and the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: For a חכם you uncover the right shoulder, for an אב בית דין the left, and for a נשיא both shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a חכם, a person uncovers the right shoulder. For an אב בית דין, the left. For a נשיא, both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about another mourning act: uncovering the shoulder. Each level of leader gets a different way of doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each step up in leadership adds to the mourning. A חכם gets one shoulder, the right. An אב בית דין gets the other shoulder, the left. The נשיא, the highest leader, gets both shoulders uncovered.

keyTerms.meaning: Uncovers, pulls the garment off the shoulder
A Torah scholar
The head of the court, second in rank after the נשיא
From here and from here, meaning from both sides

phrases.english: For a sage, one uncovers from the right,
for the head of the court, from the left,
for the Nasi, from here and from here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from tearing to a related mourning act, uncovering the shoulder, and sets out three levels of leaders: חכם, אב בית דין and נשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncover the right shoulder for a חכם, the left for an אב בית דין, and both for a נשיא.

steps.title: How study halls and the synagogue change when each leader dies
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that Torah study stops in more and more places depending on whether a חכם, an אב בית דין, or a נשיא died. People also switch seats in the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: When a חכם dies, his own בית מדרש stops learning. When an אב בית דין dies, all the בתי מדרש in his city stop. People go into the בית הכנסת and change their places: those who sit in the north sit in the south, and those who sit in the south sit in the north. When a נשיא dies, all the בתי מדרש everywhere stop, and the members of the בית הכנסת enter the בית הכנסת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with three more levels of public mourning. The last line is not finished here; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourning spreads wider as the leader's rank goes up. For a חכם, only his own בית מדרש stops. For an אב בית דין, every בית מדרש in his city stops, and people change seats in the בית הכנסת. For a נשיא, every בית מדרש everywhere stops.

keyTerms.meaning: Study hall where Torah is learned
Stops, takes a break from its regular learning
They change their seats
Synagogue
The חכמים taught. This opens a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the levels. For a חכם, only HIS OWN study hall stops. For an אב בית דין, every study hall in HIS CITY stops. For a נשיא, ALL study halls stop.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A sage who died: his study hall stops,
A head of court who died:
all the study halls in his city stop.

phrases.aramaic: וְנִכְנָסִין לְבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת וּמְשַׁנִּין אֶת מְקוֹמָן:
phrases.english: And they enter the synagogue and change their places:
those who sit in the north sit in the south,
those who sit in the south sit in the north.

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׂיא שֶׁמֵּת — בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת כּוּלָּן בְּטֵילִין,
phrases.english: A Nasi who died: all the study halls stop,
and the members of the synagogue enter the synagogue

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָכָם שֶׁמֵּת — בֵּית מִדְרָשׁוֹ בָּטֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps the same three levels of leaders from Step 29 and adds more ways the community mourns: stopping study and changing seats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah study stops in his own בית מדרש for a חכם, in every בית מדרש in his city for an אב בית דין (with seat changes in the בית הכנסת), and in every בית מדרש for a נשיא.
